card_quote: Narrative: Two kids, little time; does Christmas shopping online in November, picks things that will make the recipient laugh on the day. / Constraints: buys several small gifts at once, so each one has a low budget; the recipient's taste matters more than hers.
how_read: Flip-through, the way I'd judge a stocking filler. Read the first couple of pages, the How to play, then did most of round one at the kitchen table after the kids were down, and had a quick look at the bits at the back. I wasn't going to read the whole thing; it's for my brother, not me.

w1_friction.note: The example says number one is Newton's apple, then number one is actually Archimedes. Small thing, but I went back to check I hadn't skipped a page.
w1_friction.quote: ROUND 1 · № 1 Did Newton get hit by an apple?

w1_friction.note: First answer and it's a full page of small print about treatises and propositions. I wanted the punchline, not a lecture.
w1_friction.quote: its Proposition 5 gives the corollary for floating bodies

w1_friction.note: Hang on, didn't I just read this? Two pages in a row about the same apple.
w1_friction.quote: Newton himself told of the apple, according to Britannica

w1_friction.note: Moore's law turned into Dennard scaling and clock speeds. My brother might like it; I glazed over.
w1_friction.quote: a separate one, Dennard scaling, under which shrinking transistors

w1_friction.note: So the answer is basically 'nobody knows'? Bit of a let-down after guessing.
w1_friction.quote: Who first said it, and in what words, is not settled.

w1_best.why: Blood, toil, tears and sweat. I'd have bet money on the three-word version. That's the one I'd read out on Christmas Day.
The apple never hit him. Everyone knows the cartoon version, so it's an easy one to catch people out with.
Einstein's Nobel not being for relativity. I half knew it from QI but it's a good one to feel clever about.
Short and clear: Moore said every year, then two years, and the 18 months was someone else. Clean answer.
A Babylonian tablet a thousand years before Pythagoras. That's a nice 'ooh' moment.

w1_flat.why: Same apple again straight after the last one. Felt like padding.
Ends with 'disputed', so there's no satisfying reveal.
Latin sentences and friars. I don't know what Occam's razor is, so I couldn't play.
Never heard the rhyme, so there was nothing to be wrong about.
Fine, but the whole answer is that it was written as a sentence instead of a formula. Bit of a technicality.

w1_review.headline: Clever stocking filler, but heavier than it looks
w1_review.body: The idea is great and the first few questions had me guessing wrong in a way that was actually fun. The 'For ... from Certified Know-It-All' page at the front is a lovely touch for a gift. But the answers are long and quite dry, more like an encyclopedia than the QI books it reminded me of, and a few of the early ones repeat each other. Bottom line: good for the nerd in the family who reads every word, less so for a laugh round the table.

w2_review_first: It's a myth-buster quiz book, you guess true or false and turn over. Good concept and some of the answers are great to show off with, but the answer pages are walls of text. I'd give it to my brother, not to my mum.

w2_lost.why: The very first answer was so long I nearly closed it there.
The computer chip one lost me halfway, too technical.
Round two started with Latin and I put it down to sort the washing.

w2_read_aloud.why: Everyone will say 'blood, sweat and tears' and be wrong. Perfect for the table.
Kids would enjoy the apple one too.
Barbra Streisand suing over a photo of her house sounds like a good gossip story.
Hot water freezing faster always starts an argument in our house.
Toast landing butter-side down, that's a proper Christmas-morning one.

w2_cut.why: Uncertainty principle. I don't even know what the question means.
Thucydides trap, 12 of 16 rivalries. Sounds like homework.
An acronym from nuclear strategy. Not a fun family question.
Maxwell's equations. My brother might know; nobody else at the table would.

w2_book2: If the second one was another 250 pages of small print with the same long answers, I'd get him something else.
